### (b) why these changes
The plan's §4 design splits #494 into three phases with one driver each:

- **Phase 1 re-runs the inline-444 predictors under canonical recipe** because the inline analysis (`eval_results/issue_444/persona_distance_topic/results.json` `config`) ran at `js_r=6, js_max_tok=48`, NOT the canonical `R=8 / max_tokens=256` defined in `.claude/rules/persona-distance-metrics.md` L18-L34. Pooling #494's #192 numbers (which WILL be at canonical) against the inline-444 numbers at a different recipe would conflate recipe drift with substrate effect. The fix is to recompute #444 at canonical alongside #192. cosine_a / bystander_logprob / fact_slice_js are recipe-independent by construction (no sampling), so the consistency gate at the end of Phase 1 doubles as a regression check — if those three quantities diverge from inline by >1e-4 there's a code-path bug in the recompute, not a recipe effect.
- **Phase 2 is the substantive value-add** the inline-444 analysis did not do: extend the same predictor recipe to a second substrate (#192's positive-only Lin/Pavlek rig) with a different fact, different teacher, different bystander panel, different training regime. The 4 predictors per cell test the open-questions trailer's reference-frame hypothesis on a within-rig + across-rig basis the single-substrate inline analysis cannot. Probe subset n=30 (vs full 150) is justified in plan §4.2: DV resolution is 8 cells not 150, so larger probe counts only tighten the per-cell predictor mean for diminishing returns at the re-analysis budget (per-cell SE 30^-1/2 ≈ 0.18 vs 150^-1/2 ≈ 0.08 for 5× compute; #444 ran at n=60 so #192 at n=30 is only 1.4× noisier per cell).
- **Phase 3 is pooled + per-stratum** because substrates are heterogeneous (#192 is positive-only with leakage clustered tightly ~58-65%; #444's three contrastive recipes have leakage spread 0.02-0.99) and pooling them blindly conflates two leakage regimes. The plan pre-registered per-stratum Spearman + pooled Spearman with substrate as a fixed factor; the cluster-aware bootstrap (sample-with-replacement within each substrate) preserves stratification, avoiding the unstratified bootstrap's bias toward whichever stratum has the wider spread. Partial Spearman tests the trailer's claim that the prior survives controlling for distance and distance does not survive controlling for prior.

The single-script-per-phase architecture matches the plan §4.8 smoke/sweep parity statement — no multi-cell launcher, no subprocess dispatch, smoke IS production with `--smoke` flags that reduce to 1 cell.

## (b) Considered but not done
- **Off-topic null reference (Betley probe set across both substrates).** Plan §5 lists this as a separate condition; §9 auto-descope order has it as priority-1 drop. I did NOT wire it in this round — the headline path is the on-topic predictors, and the auto-descope says drop off-topic first if compute runs over. If the headline pass shows the on-topic story is interesting, the off-topic null is a 1h GPU-h follow-up on the same scripts (add `--off-topic-probes` flag, fetch from `issue404_common.fetch_preregistered_probes`). Defer.
- **Per-probe-family JS slice for #444 A-family.** The plan calls out `js_sliced_by_probe_type.png` as part of the exploratory dump; the current Phase 1 driver aggregates JS to a single per-(persona, recipe) value, not per-family. The Phase 3 figure for this is a stub (a labeled placeholder). A per-family slice is a Phase-1 driver code-path: change `js_vs_reference_canonical` to return per-probe JS, group by `build_reformulation_probes` keys. I left it out because (a) the plan's headline tests don't require it and (b) the inline-444 analysis didn't slice it either, so cross-comparison stays cleanest at the aggregate level.
- **Off-loading the HF model BEFORE vLLM via process fork.** The current pattern is `del model; gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache(); torch.cuda.synchronize()`. Per CLAUDE.md gotchas, vLLM worker subprocesses can survive a `del` and re-allocate freed GPU memory. I followed the inline-444 pattern (single Python process, sequential HF → vLLM phases within one script) because the inline-444 scripts run cleanly that way. If the production launch hits an OOM at the vLLM phase, fall back to splitting Phase 1 into two SSH-invoked subprocesses (one for HF predictors, one for the vLLM prior). Flagged in (d) needs-human-eyeball.
- **Pre-computed bystander_logprob reuse from inline-444.** The inline-444 `eval_results/issue_444/bystander_logprob/logprob_results.json` is recipe-independent and could be read out instead of re-computed. I chose to re-compute because (a) the plan §4.1 explicitly calls for the recompute as a consistency check, (b) re-running the vLLM teacher-force on 6 personas × 239 teach rows is ~5 min (a tiny fraction of the budget), and (c) the consistency-check block then doubles as a code-path validation.
- **Storing the per-probe JS values + per-response sampled tokens.** I store the per-cell aggregate but not the per-probe / per-response trajectories. Per-probe JS would enable a probe-family slice (see above); per-response samples would enable a downstream analyzer to spot-check the on-policy distribution. Skipped for budget; if the analyzer needs per-probe JS, re-run with a `--keep-per-probe` flag.

## (d) Needs human eyeball
- **The vLLM-after-HF GPU-handoff pattern.** Phase 1 + Phase 2 each load the HF model first (cosine a/b + JS + fact-slice), then `_drop_model(model)` and load vLLM for the bystander prior. The `_drop_model` helper does `del model; gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache(); torch.cuda.synchronize()` — the inline-444 pattern. Per CLAUDE.md "vLLM worker-subprocess teardown" gotcha, this can fail if vLLM worker subprocesses survive across phases; the inline-444 scripts didn't hit this because they ran ONE phase per script invocation. If the production smoke shows the vLLM phase OOMs after the HF phase, the fix is to split each Phase into two `nohup`-chained scripts.
- **The Phase 1 consistency-gate tolerance (1e-4).** The inline-444 numbers come from a different HF Transformers + vLLM version snapshot; deterministic forward passes with bfloat16 weights can drift by ~1e-5 across HF version bumps. 1e-4 is the plan-specified tolerance. If the gate FAILs by a hair (say 1e-4 < diff < 1e-3), that's a version drift not a code bug; the appropriate response is to widen the tolerance + flag the inline-444 numbers as "from an older snapshot" in the clean-result rather than block Phase 2.
- **#192 Arm B teach prompt overlap.** The Qwen-default teach prompt (`"You are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant."`) overlaps lexically with the `assistant` bystander (`"You are a helpful assistant."`) and is similar to `no_system`. The plan §4.2 + §5 + §8 (Risks row) flag this; the analyzer should report Arm B with-and-without the `assistant` bystander as a sensitivity check. The driver doesn't apply this filter — it reports all 4 bystanders per arm.
- **The `js_sliced_by_probe_type` placeholder figure.** Currently emits a text-stub PNG; the analyzer should either populate from a per-family JS rerun (~30 min on the same driver with a `--per-family` flag) or remove from the clean-result figure list.
- **Phases 1+2 smoke runs are still pending on pod-494** — local CPU validation covered Phase 3 + import/argparse/HF-fetch checks; the GPU-side smoke (cosine_a byte-identity check, finite/range checks on cosine_b + JS + fact_slice_js, vLLM bystander_logprob byte-identity) fires only on a real GPU.
